sources.title: Emu War
sources.cites: Johnson, M. (2006) 'Feathered foes': soldier settlers and Western Australia's 'Emu War' of 1932, Journal of Australian Studies 30(88), doi:10.1080/14443050609388083; Sunday Herald (1953) for the Meredith quote

sources.title: Emu: national symbols and ecological limits (in Boom and Bust, CSIRO Publishing 2009)

claims.text: In late 1932 the Australian army was sent with machine guns to cull emus in Western Australia's wheat belt (the 'Emu War').
claims.quote: The Seventh Heavy Battery of the Royal Australian Artillery brought two Lewis guns and 10 000 rounds of ammunition to the 'war' (Robin); cull roughly 20,000 emus using machine guns (Britannica)

claims.label: the army withdrew
claims.text: 'Lost' is the popular framing: there was no declared war; the unit was withdrawn without solving the problem.
claims.quote: A crestfallen field force therefore withdrew from the combat area after about a month.

claims.text: After WWI, discharged veterans were given land to farm in Western Australia.
claims.quote: Following World War I, large numbers of discharged veterans who served in the war were given land by the Australian government to take up farming within Western Australia

claims.label: about 20,000
claims.text: About 20,000 emus moved into the wheat-growing area and damaged crops.
claims.quote: the planted crop in 1932 supported 20 000 emus in an area of about 40 square miles near Southern Cross (Robin); a marauding emu population of at least 20,000 had been devastating farms (Australian Geographic)

claims.text: The force: Major G.P.W. Meredith, two soldiers, two Lewis guns and 10,000 rounds.
claims.quote: Maj. Gwynydd Purves Wynne-Aubrey Meredith in command, Sgt. S. McMurray, and Gunner J. O'Halloran ... two Lewis machine guns and 10,000 rounds of ammunition

claims.text: The emus split into small groups, frustrating the gunners.
claims.quote: The Emu command had evidently ordered guerrilla tactics, and its unwieldy army soon split up into innumerable small units.

claims.text: An ambush on more than 1,000 emus failed when a gun jammed.
claims.quote: more than 1,000 emus were spotted heading towards their position...The gun jammed after only 12 birds were killed.

claims.text: A machine gun mounted on a truck failed because the truck could not keep up with the emus.
claims.quote: a later attempt to mount a machine-gun on a truck fell apart when it was made apparent that the vehicle could not keep up

claims.label: the major's own count
claims.text: Meredith reported 986 kills using 9,860 rounds: ten rounds per bird. These are his own claimed figures and are disputed.
claims.quote: he claimed 986 confirmed kills with 9,860 rounds, at a rate of exactly 10 rounds per confirmed kill (Wikipedia); 986 emus were killed ... though these figures remain disputed (Britannica)

claims.text: Meredith: 'They can face machine guns with the invulnerability of tanks.'
claims.quote: They can face machine guns with the invulnerability of tanks.

claims.text: Meredith was recalled on 10 December 1932; the emus remained.
claims.quote: Meredith was recalled on 10 December, and in his report, he claimed 986 confirmed kills with 9,860 rounds.
capable of running nearly 30 miles (50 km) per hour
claims.note: True, but not used: the script says 'faster than the truck' instead. Kept as an example of a rejected (unused) claim.

myths.myth: Australia formally declared war on emus.
myths.truth: It was a military cull operation; 'war' is press and popular framing.

open_questions: Exact kill count is disputed; Meredith's figures are self-reported.
